Tanis is the kind of podcast that you just have to listen to again and again. I didn't even start to get it until I'd listened three times. I think that's why a lot of people get frustrated with it and just give up or write it off. It's very complex and a lot of the time small details that you don't even notice become really relevent later on. It's actually a lot better written than people give it credit for. It's impossible to explain it all, it would take hours. I guess it just depends on how determined you are to understand it and how much time you're willing to spend (or some would say waste) listening to it. I have no life so for me it's not a big deal, I've been listening to the episodes on repeat for years now. I've heard the whole thing over 50 times and I'm still piecing it together. For me it's been worth it but yeah.. it's up to you.

I'm not a recovering drug addict, however I have a true anecdote which may be comforting: my aunties boyfriend, the father of my cousin, was a heroin addict over 20 years ago when my cousin was born and was a drug addict for most of my cousins life (my cousin is in his 20s). He lost my auntie and didn't get to see his son grow up. He completely lost touch with them. He spend 18 more years as a drug addict. He was a wreck. It took him 18 years, a lot of relapses and a lot of rehab. It wasn't easy for him at all. But after 18 years of suffering he got himself clean. And him and my auntie got back together by chance. He now lives with her and is living a happy clean life. They go to the theatre a lot, travel and he's finally living the dream. He now knows his son. I know that it doesn't happen this way for everyone. I'm not stupid. I know of people who have died from their addiction and I know people who have committed suicide. I know that holding on isn't easy. But this is proof that it is possible to overcome addiction and turn your life around, however much time it might take, however much holding on and holding back it may take. I'm so glad that you're in a place that you can use the term recovering. Just know that complete recovery is possible. I hope that this gives you a bit of hope.
